figures.caption: G1 negative control: max|u| of a resting two-layer column vs interface offset. The closed-form profile (dashed) leaves a rho*g imbalance at partial cells; the balanced discrete profile (solid) holds to round-off.

figures.caption: G3/G4: dam-break surge front against Martin & Moyce (1952) at several resolutions (left) and the liquid-volume drift of each leg (right, dotted = 0.1 % gate).

figures.caption: Liquid-fraction field of every dam-break leg at the final time. The alpha = 0.5 contour shows how sharp the surge (and how much of it) each resolution transports.

figures.caption: Analytic anchors. Left: the gate surface of the tall Martin & Moyce column falls in free fall until the rarefaction returns (A1). Right: the shallow dam-break front against the Ritter solution (A2).

figures.caption: Kinematic attainability of the digitised Martin & Moyce points under the case's own scaling: the mean acceleration 2s/t^2 that each point implies, in units of g. Only the very early points exceed the 2 g bound, so the front gate is taken at t* >= 2.
figures.name: fig5-mm-reference-kinematics.png

front_onset.note: the front cannot leave at t = 0 in the discrete solve because the pressure head is built incrementally from p = 0; the measured onset is the size of that transient

G3_mass_conservation.criterion: |dV|/V0 <= 0.001 on the PLIC legs (the donor-cell control is reported separately)

G4a_freefall_surface.reference: h(t) = 2a - g t^2/2 (kinematic free fall, t < a/sqrt(2 g a))

G4b_ritter_front.criterion: |x_f - 2 sqrt(g h0) t| / (2 sqrt(g h0) t) <= 0.15
G4b_ritter_front.profile_note: L2 relative error of eta(x) at the last snapshot, over the interior of the Ritter wedge
G4b_ritter_front.reference: Ritter (1892) dry-bed dam break, shallow-water theory

G4c_martin_moyce_front.note: t* = 1 is reported in 3.2 but excluded from the gate: the digitised point needs more than 2 g (see 3.4)

martin_moyce_kinematics.verdict: the digitised series contains points that a gravity-driven collapse cannot reach under the stated scaling (they need more than 2 g); those early points cannot be used as an accuracy gate

evaluation.criterion: |x_f - 2 sqrt(g h0) t| / (2 sqrt(g h0) t) <= 0.15
